newsitem.title: UK: Vodafone to connect with NatGrid.
newsitem.headline: Vodafone to connect with NatGrid.

text.p: Vodafone Group, Britain's biggest mobile phones firm, said on Thursday that it planned to use the high voltage electricity pylons of the National Grid's power network as sites for new "base stations" to operate its network.
These mast-like structures vary in height from about 18 metres to 45 metres. Up to now, Vodafone has installed many of them on roof tops, paying landlords a fee.
A spokeswoman declined to divulge how much the National Grid was charging for the potential use of over 21,000 pylons, many in rural areas.
The group, which needs to expand its coverage, hopes the masts will be less of an eyesore than stand-alone structures.

After 12 months of successful trials, David Jones, chief executive of the National Grid, said: "We see it as an ideal arrangement for both parties and an opportunity to minimise impact on the environment."
Vodafone plans about 50 new sites per month, although it can share those of other operators and few of those planned will be stand-alone structures, the spokeswoman noted.
The National Grid also has its own telecommunications business -- Energis -- which uses its power pylons.

It has been conducting an open search for an international partner for the network. Some analysts say Energis, which has no current direct link to end-users, could carry a price-tag of up to 1.5 billion stg.
